extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists and editorial staff (including text, TV, picture, online and freelance contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Company-level editorial and ethical standards for Reuters journalists worldwide, setting requirements for accuracy, sourcing, independence, impartiality, visual integrity, conflicts of interest, use of AI, and related newsroom behaviours. Applies to reporters, editors, photographers, videographers and other editorial staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Trust Principles in all activities related to Reuters News.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles underpin Reuters' independence, accuracy and impartiality; they should govern all editorial decisions and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold accuracy sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is at the heart of what we do. It is our job to get it first but it is above all our job to get it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy, as well as balance, always takes precedence over speed. Before publishing, think how you would withstand a challenge or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek fair comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek fair comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give subjects of stories the opportunity to state their position; allegations should not be portrayed as fact and charges should not be conveyed as guilt without substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct errors transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters rectifies errors promptly, clearly and comprehensively whether in a story, a caption, a graphic or a script; be transparent about corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for balance and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for balance and freedom from bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be scrupulously fair and balanced; avoid taking sides; choose words carefully to avoid implying judgments (e.g., 'fears', 'insists', 'failed to comment').

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest to a manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any activity or relationship could give rise to a perception of conflict, raise it with your manager; the list of possible conflicts is not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unattributed opinion in news
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid injecting unattributed opinion in a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News stories must remain fact-based; opinions belong in clearly labeled analysis or opinion pieces and must be properly identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fabricate or plagiarise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fabricate or plagiarise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication or plagiarism undermines credibility and may lead to disciplinary measures including dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not materially alter images or footage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not alter still images or video footage beyond the methods normally used to prepare content for editorial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual journalism must reflect unaltered reality; do not use generative AI to create or enhance imagery. Minor editorial prep is allowed but not changes that alter reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay for information or accept bribes or trade on privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pay for information or accept a bribe or trade on privileged information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buying information or accepting inducements is unethical and grounds for dismissal; avoid appearance of impropriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy priority and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy always comes first; it's better to be late than wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check information wherever possible; think about how claims would hold up to challenge; verify facts and sources; when in doubt, delay publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters is transparent about errors and must rectify them promptly and comprehensively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections apply to stories, captions, graphics and scripts. Be clear about what has changed and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing: prefer named sources and honesty in sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: A named source is generally preferable to an unnamed source; accuracy entails honesty in sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named sources wherever possible and press sources to go on the record; we remain liable for accuracy and legal risks even with named sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing: use unnamed sources only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters will use unnamed sources where necessary when they provide information of market or public interest that is not available on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnamed sources must be judged on track record, position and motive; weigh credibility and take responsibility for accuracy. Single-source stories require special authorisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing: ground rules, notes and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: When talking to sources, make the ground rules clear and take notes; where allowed, record interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about on-the-record vs background, keep good records and preserve evidence of sourcing where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing: cross-check and seek multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-check information wherever possible; two or more sources are better than one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to disprove as well as prove your story; talk to sources on all sides; give context and be explicit about what you don't know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing: confidentiality and disclosure to managers
rubrics_metrics.description: A source’s compact is with Reuters, not the reporter; protect confidentiality but disclose sources to supervisors on legitimate editorial grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protecting source confidentiality is paramount, but supervisors may need to know the source in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes are sacrosanct and must never be altered other than to delete a redundant word or clause provided the deletion does not alter the sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective quoting can be unbalanced; quotes must be representative; consult senior staff if considering running an awkward quote verbatim; translations should preserve tone and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflecting reality (language and visual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and stories must reflect reality; avoid hype, sensationalism or language that skews perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with words like 'flood' or 'surge' that may exaggerate; visual journalism must not add to or detract from reality; fabrication may lead to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines and bylines accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines should indicate the writer was at the dateline; use datelines only where staff/freelancers are on the spot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters/freelancers who contributed should be credited in an additional-reporting line with name and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly attribute material that is not ours, whether in story, photograph or moving images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sources clearly (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video', 'U.S. Army Photo'); 'handout' alone is insufficient and may invite plagiarism charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rumours carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to report facts, not rumours; if rumours affect markets, seek to verify or knock them down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only in exceptional circumstances where markets move rapidly may a story be moved before full verification; be cautious and explain context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic images and obscenity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish graphic images or obscene language gratuitously; there must be a valid news reason and often senior-editor signoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether material is necessary for understanding; packaged videos must have 'Warning: Graphic Content' and RAW videos must include a warning in scripts and slates; be mindful of differing market thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence: avoid conflicts and maintain statelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence is essential; avoid conflicts of interest or any perception of bias that would undermine impartial reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If potential conflicts arise, raise with your manager; independence applies to interactions with companies, institutions and customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal investments restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow investments held by you or immediate family to influence your work; do not report on or edit stories about entities in which you have an interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid trading that creates the reality or optics of a conflict; follow Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct on investments and material nonpublic information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare financial interests and follow Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare financial interests and adhere to Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct's requirements on personal investments and access to material nonpublic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to follow the code is subject to disciplinary procedures in the relevant location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work outside Reuters policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not engage in paid work outside Reuters unless you have manager permission in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission is routinely given if activities don't affect Reuters; NewsGuild U.S. members have limited exceptions; disclose and seek permission for book, article, speaking, or commercial photography work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking back with sources limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit stories, scripts or images to sources to vet before publication; checking back for verification is allowed but must not give sources chance to retract or alter materially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist requests to approve quotes; if you must submit quotes for approval, do not agree to material changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts, hospitality and entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept payment, gift, service or benefit from a news source or contact except nominal traditional gifts; hospitality must be newsworthy and within reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a gift of more than nominal value is received, decline or surrender to your manager; do not accept junkets or hospitality that could create obligations to sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation offers
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard position is that Reuters pays its own way; if free travel/accommodation is offered consult your manager and normally reimburse the provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission normally given only when story warrants coverage; in exceptional circumstances (remote locations, war zones) managers' permission required and reimbursement should be made when practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: No bribery or facilitation payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under no circumstances take or offer payment for a news story; Reuters does not permit facilitation payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conduct is a grave breach of ethics and may result in dismissal or legal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence within Reuters (corporate separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial independence is maintained by the Trust Principles and the Founders Share Company Board; do not alter coverage to help sales or commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-editorial colleague raises a complaint about balance, examine the complaint fairly and apply sound news judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may submit Reuters work to awards judged by journalists with manager approval; submissions to contests not judged by journalists require senior approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not produce Reuters work primarily for awards; submissions to potentially self-serving sponsors are generally not permitted and require explicit approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying as journalists and no deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters journalists do not obtain news by deception or pass themselves off as something other than a journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asked directly, identify yourself as a Reuters journalist; rare exceptions may be considered in the interests of news gathering but should follow code and common sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting from the Internet standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same standards of sourcing, identification and verification to online reporting as to other newsgathering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use material that cannot be sourced and verified; take the same precautions online as in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must not participate in insider trading or tipping based on material non-public information obtained through employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information that could affect market price is material regardless of being factual or speculative; treat employer-obtained information as non-public until widely disseminated and absorbed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with sources: professional cultivation and detachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate sources professionally but avoid relationships that create bias or the perception of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be polite and fair; avoid spending disproportionate leisure time with sources; disclose romantic or family attachments with news sources to managers; do not quote family members to avoid perception of favouritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with customers: maintain editorial/commercial separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a clear line between editorial and commercial functions when dealing with customers who are also news sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not negotiate sales contracts or discuss commercial terms as a journalist; maintain professional journalism behaviours with clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with people in news: sensitivity and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat victims with sensitivity, avoid needless pain and offence, seek clear facts and avoid sensationalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to spin and bias, including your own; apply integrity, impartiality, persistence, accountability and humility so stories can be defended to sources and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with competitors ethically
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain information about competitors ethically; do not make deals on coverage or trade material that is improper or illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge competitors' exclusive reporting when appropriate; cooperate only when it reduces risk to life or is in mutual interest (e.g., staff safety).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling complaints promptly and professionally
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate complaints about accuracy, balance or ethics promptly and handle them at senior level when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge complaints that can't be immediately resolved; escalate when necessary; keep a constructive attitude and avoid hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests from authorities for unpublished material
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer any requests for published or unpublished Reuters content from authorities to a senior editor and alert editorial legal team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between published and unpublished material; do not voluntarily hand over unpublished material; consider lawful challenges to subpoenas to protect staff and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with each other: teamwork and respectful workplace
rubrics_metrics.description: Teamwork across disciplines is required; staff should be able to raise standards and ethics concerns without fear of reprisal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share information and ideas responsibly; maintain a workplace free from harassment and treat all with dignity and respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting internal incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Report serious incidents involving harm or risk to staff, problems with stories/images, hoaxes or allegations of improper behaviour to supervisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt reporting helps managers and other bureaus spot trends and protect staff and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life outside Reuters: avoid blurring professional/private lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a clear distinction between professional activities and private opinions when using company systems or representing yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid expressing political opinion or investment advice on company systems; use private email for personal correspondence; do not use Reuters identity to obtain special benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias: park nationality and politics
rubrics_metrics.description: Park nationality and politics at the door and strive for neutrality in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of unconscious stereotyping and country stereotypes; use neutral language and include relevant context rather than gratuitous descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take no side, tell all sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Never identify with any side in an issue; reflect all sides in text and visual stories while applying judgement on space allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectivity doesn't require equal space for all sides; give opportunities for response and avoid implying guilt or judgment through language choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion and analysis separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish clearly between fact-based news and clearly labeled opinion pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must not express personal opinions in news stories, voiced video, scripts or workplace blogs; columns and point-of-view pieces must be clearly labeled and underpinned by expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discriminatory language and stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inappropriate references to gender, ethnicity, religion, culture, appearance, age and sexual orientation and be sensitive to unconscious stereotyping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral language and avoid gratuitous references to appearance or identity; include such details only when relevant and placed appropriately in copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not give investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not express personal views on the merits of investments; reports containing value judgments must be sourced to a named third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters reports news and does not give investment advice; local laws may prohibit offering advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Thomson Reuters procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Extreme care must be taken when reporting on Thomson Reuters and affiliates to avoid any hint of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such stories must be seen before publication by senior editors and the Global Editor for Ethics and Standards; include comment from a company spokesman and follow policy on pickup and market relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and community activity guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not give support to political parties or identify Reuters with any political group; staff should be sensitive to activities outside work that could create perceptions of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common sense, the Trust Principles and consult managers in doubt; Reuters may require reassignment if perceptions of conflict arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity and diversity commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat employees fairly regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation etc.; embrace diversity in the newsroom and journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for jobs, training and promotion should be based on skills and relevant requirements in accordance with local law; diversity enriches journalism and should be encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media interviews and speaking engagements rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews and speaking engagements require prior manager and communications-team approval and correspondents must not give personal opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be from credible outlets; Reuters services take precedence; payment should not be sought or accepted; staff must avoid embarrassment to Reuters or jeopardising access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference participation principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in conferences requires editorial approval; journalists should stick to facts and avoid panels where panelists have paid to participate or where the event aims to sell a product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may appear only once a year at a company's conferences; reporters following a company should not participate in that company's events; payment for participation or expenses should not usually be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial intelligence and generative AI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace AI opportunities but maintain editorial accountability and transparency; do not use GenAI to create or enhance imagery and use caution with AI-generated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All facts, sources and claims generated by AI must be independently verified and fact-checked; do not upload Reuters or third-party content to non-approved external tools; seek guidance from Ethics and Standards and Legal when in doubt.
